purpose: Define only the one-time first initialization contract that brings a brand-new resolver D1 to the exact resolver schema and canonical d1_migrations ledger required by D3 promotion preflight.

immutable_release_authority.remote_bootstrap_input_rule: Canonical migration bytes for external first bootstrap must come only from a successfully verified immutable accepted-main resolver release artifact, never from an arbitrary mutable working tree.
required_future_ceremony: Identify one exact accepted-main resolver release.
Extract that release's exact migrations/resolver-d1 inventory.
Build bootstrap SQL only from those extracted migration bytes.
Record the verified release identity and migration-manifest digest in metadata-only evidence.
Require D3 promotion later to accept the remote resolver ledger against the same release.
immutable_release_authority.local_development_exception: Working-tree migrations may be used only for disposable local development and self-tests; they are insufficient authority for external bootstrap.
external_bootstrap_eligibility: The immutable resolver release used for external first bootstrap must be produced from accepted-main source that already contains the accepted first-bootstrap implementation and compatible resolver release migration validator.
Current historical release artifacts may be used as reference evidence but are not automatically bootstrap-eligible after this authority.
After implementation is merged, external bootstrap must use a new exact accepted-main resolver release produced from that implementation SHA.

out_of_scope: D4 migration compatibility or fail-forward policy

rules: Local parity does not require or include Cloudflare's _cf_KV table.
Database A applies only validated resolver migration SQL and does not create d1_migrations.
Database B applies generated bootstrap SQL.

required_rules: A pre-import Wrangler schema query must prove that the complete non-sqlite SQLite schema inventory exactly equals accepted_platform_owned_schema_inventory.
No application-owned table, index, trigger, or view may exist before import.
A malformed, missing, duplicate, or additional platform-owned schema object rejects the target.
An existing d1_migrations table rejects the target as non-fresh.
Any existing resolver application table rejects the target as non-fresh.
The generated SQL guard executes before ledger or application DDL as defense in depth, but does not replace exact remote fresh-target evidence validation.

migration_inventory.ordering: deterministic lexical order by canonical filename, equivalent to ascending numeric prefix
required_rejections: malformed UTF-8 or malformed migration input
release_validation_compatibility: Future bootstrap implementation and accepted resolver release validation must use compatible migration-inventory acceptance semantics.
A resolver release whose migration inventory is rejected by first bootstrap is not first-bootstrap eligible.

canonical_migration_ledger.name: d1_migrations
canonical_migration_ledger.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE "d1_migrations" (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT UNIQUE, applied_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP NOT NULL);

semantics.id: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT; establishes application order
semantics.name: TEXT UNIQUE; stores the exact canonical resolver migration filename

rules: The bootstrap creates this canonical repository ledger; no resolver-specific alternate ledger is permitted.
Each exact resolver migration produces exactly one ledger row after that migration is applied.
Ledger names and rows must be in exact migration inventory order.

current_expected_query.sql: SELECT name FROM d1_migrations ORDER BY id;

construction_order: each exact resolver migration in inventory order
one exact d1_migrations INSERT after each corresponding migration
determinism: Identical accepted migration inputs produce byte-identical bootstrap SQL.
The bootstrap SHA-256 is computed over those exact bytes.
The generated SQL is a one-time fresh-D1 ceremony, not an idempotent migration runner.

local_parity_proof.database_a: Use a disposable normal local SQLite database; apply the exact validated resolver migration SQL sequentially and do not create d1_migrations.
local_parity_proof.database_b: Use a separate disposable normal local SQLite database; apply generated bootstrap SQL.
must_prove_equal: application-owned table, index, trigger, and view definitions
database_b_additional_checks: Its schema exactly equals canonical_migration_ledger.schema_sql semantics.
Its ordered names exactly equal the validated migration inventory.
local_parity_proof.derivation_rule: Derive schema parity from the migration inventory wherever possible; retain only established repository security invariants as explicit checks.

conceptual_order: Create one dedicated resolver D1 externally.
Read-only inspect the exact fresh-target schema.
Verify immutable release identity and extract its exact resolver migration bytes.
Generate deterministic resolver bootstrap SQL from those exact extracted release bytes.
Import that SQL remotely with the pinned Wrangler toolchain.
Query d1_migrations and verify the exact ordered ledger.
Prove the expected resolver schema inventory.
Prove replay rejection on a disposable proof target or through an accepted bounded proof mechanism.
Only then mark the resolver D1 eligible for D3 promotion preflight.

validator_rejections: extra, missing, reordered, or malformed fresh-target schema row

release_identity_validation: resolver_source_commit_sha must equal the source SHA verified from the immutable release archive used as bootstrap input.
resolver_migration_manifest_sha256 must equal the verified migration-manifest digest for the extracted bootstrap input bytes.
resolver_release_id must identify that same verified immutable release.
A mismatch between release source, migration digest, release identity, or bootstrap inputs fails validation.

promotion_compatibility.required_preflight_query: SELECT name FROM d1_migrations ORDER BY id;
promotion_compatibility.required_preflight_behavior: Compare remote names with the immutable resolver release migration inventory.
promotion_compatibility.bootstrap_purpose: Only make a brand-new resolver D1, from the same verified immutable release, reach the exact state required by that read-only promotion preflight.

d3_d4_boundary.non_fresh_resolver_database_action: Reject and hand off to future D4 policy.
forbidden: automatically apply pending migrations during promotion

proposed_roots: dedicated permanent checker and metadata-only evidence files

resolver_release_validator_alignment.bounded_reason: The future implementation may tighten resolver release migration inventory validation only as required to enforce the same canonical contiguous-from-0001 contract used by first bootstrap.
constraints: No weakening of release artifact validation.
No reuse of an old immutable release after validator or source changes.
Implementation merge must produce a new accepted-main resolver release.
External bootstrap ceremony must consume a release created from accepted implementation source, not a pre-authority or pre-implementation release.

future_implementation.alternative: A later reviewed implementation may reuse or generalize scripts/cloudflare-d1-bootstrap.py only if it preserves accepted catalog D3A semantics and keeps resolver invocation explicit and separate.
required_negative_tests: evidence claiming user data or secret material involved
